entry.title: BGP Route Flap Management: Effective Prevention in 3 Steps
entry.summary:
Introduction to BGP Route Flap Issues: Why is the Network's Pulse Irregular?
BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) is a massive routing protocol that forms the backbone of the internet. For many network administrators, BGP is like a black box that should not be touched as long as it works. However, especially in large and complex networks, encountering a situation called BGP route flap can pose a serious threat to network stability. Route flap is a condition where a prefix (i.e., a block of IP addresses) is continuously added and removed from BGP tables, causing routing information to "fluctuate." This situation can lead to network performance degradation, latency, packet loss, and even service interruptions. In my experience, BGP route flap issues are often overlooked or seen as just a temporar…
